To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the magnitude and the phase of low-order converter generated voltage harmonicity are dependent on the operating point of the converter and the phase of converter current, which is a function of the converter operating point, respectively.
the magnitude and the phase of low-order harmonic components of the converter generated voltage are dependent on the operating point and the current phase of the fundamental, respectively.

a sequence-domain (SD) harmonic modeling procedure for a grid-connected voltage source converter is developed and the modeling procedure is used to make power quality (Pq) assessments of a 3MW Type-IV (Type-IV) wind turbine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an SD harmonic model of a Type-IV wind converter and the use of the SD harmonic model for PQ assessment of Type-IV turbines and power plants.
the development and validation of a sequence domain harmonic model of a voltage source converter (VSC) in a grid-connected type IV wind turbine.
the development of an SD harmonic model for Type-IV wind farms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the harmonic model developed in the present study can be used for harmonic load flow computations and PQ assessments of Type IV wind turbine.
the SD harmonic model is an effective method to decouple converter generated voltage harmons from voltage harmonics of the external grid.
the proposed harmonic model is a powerful tool in the assessment of the PQ of grid-connected Type-IV wind power systems, and can be applied for a variety of applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed SD harmonic model can accurately predict the magnitude and phase angle of converter generated voltage and current harmonics for Type-IV wind-turbines.
we have developed a sequence domain model for the voltage source converter in a type-IV wind turbine and used it in a harmonic load flow to assess the impact on the grid of the type-IV wind turbines.
a sequence domain (SD), time domain (TD), and frequency domain (FD) harmonic model of grid-connected voltage-source converters (VSC) is presented.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a Type-IV wind-turbine can generate low-order odd voltage harmonics that are decoupled from the grid.
the magnitude and the phase of low-order voltage harmonics in a Type-IV wind farm are determined by the converter operating point.
the harmonic behavior of Type-IV turbines is different from Type-I and Type-II wind turbines, and the harmonic behavior is dependent on the converter current phase.
